recommendation: Keep the empty audit commit. No core follow-up is needed; any future edits to these clinical-status code definitions should be handled through UTG/THO unless a later Jira changes core binding behavior.
issue_request: FHIR-26464 was Published/Persuasive with Modification for R5 and asked Patient Care to clarify Condition.clinicalStatus definitions for active, recurrence, relapse, inactive, remission, and resolved so they cover conditions or situations, significant/appreciable/negligible risk, and examples such as food insecurity and alcoholism.
initial_application: Commit 0d382da235aa42d53fc007e433ee8627ccbf82a1 applied the approved definitions to the former core source/condition/codesystem-condition-clinical.xml. Commit 5c0494aacfd0b8bd52bc72c587aa89d0a64246f8 later removed that CodeSystem from core as UTG-owned terminology content.
additional_context: Current core keeps Condition active in source/fhir.ini and binds Condition.clinicalStatus required to ValueSet/condition-clinical, which includes http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/condition-clinical. UP-279, the UTG proposal for the same definitions, was withdrawn after noting the terminology source-of-truth commit already existed. The current terminology.hl7.org CodeSystem contains the FHIR-26464 definitions, plus the later unknown code from the separate FHIR-29409/UP-280 family.
reconciliation: No FHIR core source file was changed. Reintroducing or editing a core CodeSystem would be wrong because the current core build delegates these code definitions to THO, and THO already matches the FHIR-26464 resolution.

related_jiras.note: UTG proposal for the FHIR-26464 code definition updates was withdrawn because the terminology source-of-truth commit already existed.
Later Condition.clinicalStatus issue added the unknown code through UP-280 and is already separately audited on the combined branch; it does not alter the FHIR-26464 definitions.
